cover.title: Design transport as close to reality as possible.
cover.lede: Faced with the energy transition and pressure on resources, Pool4ward supports companies from engineering to contracting to control their costs, reduce their risks and secure their transport capacity.

stakes.title: Transport is not an interchangeable service.
stakes.lede: Buying at the best price assumes the offer is the same everywhere. It is not: what you can move, when, with what and by whom depends on six realities on the ground.

flows.name: Flows
flows.body: Volumes and recurrence: they decide what can be pooled and what is contracted over time.

slots.name: Time windows
slots.body: Dock windows and lead times: they decide which deliveries can be chained.

drivers.name: Drivers
drivers.body: Availability and driving time: a scarce resource that bounds rotations.

equipment.name: Equipment
equipment.body: Pallets, bulk, containers: what can travel together, and in what.

energy.name: Infrastructure and energy
energy.body: Terminals, charging points, networks: what the territory allows, and at what power.

commitments.name: Commitments
commitments.body: Contracts, durations, deadlines: what is already taken, and when another organisation becomes possible again.

stakes.closing: That is why we start from the ground, not from the price.

journey.title: One case, from the reality on the ground to the contract.
journey.lede: A fictitious group, four sites, six flows. Follow it end to end: what we record, the organisations we compare, what we put out to tender and then under contract.
journey.note: Demonstration case: sites, volumes and deadlines are fictitious. The diagram is not a route calculation.

capabilities.title: One continuous line, from the first study to the managed contract.
capabilities.lede: Each capability picks up what the previous one established. Each page says what it covers, and what the software really does.

datasets.title: What we know about the ground — and how far.
datasets.lede: Intermodal, shortsea, refrigerated, barge: our datasets document the sites and the services that link them. We show them as an animation — not as a directory to search.
datasets.ladderBody: A carrier listed in a dataset does not necessarily have a free truck on your corridor. We distinguish five levels of knowledge, and the animation shows only one of them: what is referenced.
datasets.posterLabel: Preview of the globe of transport services.

evidence.title: What you can verify, and what we do not claim.
evidence.lede: No client logos or testimonials here: only what can be checked.

items.name: A navigable case
items.body: The journey above takes two minutes to go through; its limits are written into it.

items.name: Sourced analyses
items.body: Our articles cite their sources and stop where the figures stop.

items.name: Displayed coverage
items.body: The datasets showcase says whether it is an example or a publication, and how old it is.

items.name: Five capabilities, with their limits
items.body: The Solutions pages tell what the software does apart from the method we apply, and say when a function is not covered.

notClaimed.title: What we do not claim
items: Track your vehicles in real time.
Guarantee a quantified saving without having read your data.
Summarise your risk in a single score.
Treat a listed carrier as an available carrier.
Cover every country and every mode equally.

contact.title: Let’s talk about your transport plan.
contact.lede: A first conversation is enough to tell whether your flows, sites and contracts lend themselves to another organisation. You have nothing to prepare.
contact.diagnostic: Prefer to start on your own? The diagnostic takes two minutes.

levers.note: Illustration: links drawn to explain, not existing services.
levers.mapLabel: Animated map of Europe. Current lever: {lever}.

referentials.title: Optimisation in touch with the field
referentials.sub: Our reference data tie every decision to the physical and economic realities of transport: networks, sites, services, capacities and market prices.
referentials.caption: Screenshots of the Pool4ward portal. Operator and carrier names are masked.

shortsea.alt: Portal screenshot: the map of shortsea services around the world.

networks.mapLabel: Animation: the rail lines and the waterways on the map of Europe.

points.line: Truck charging points and parking areas.
points.alt: Portal screenshot: the record of a truck charging site, on the map.

carriers.name: Carriers
carriers.alt: Portal screenshot: carrier records, names masked.

prices.name: Market prices
prices.line: Our cost models cross dozens of parameters with market data from contracts and spot databases, to compare every estimate with the prices actually charged.
prices.chart: Distribution of market prices, with the first quartile and the median, and three estimates positioned against that market.

referentialExplorer.title: Reference data that describe transport as it exists
referentialExplorer.lede: We rely on reference data that describe the networks, sites, services and prices of transport. They give every analysis a concrete footing, from the field to implementation.
referentialExplorer.note: Illustrative maps: indicative routes. No operator or carrier names.

services.name: Transport services
services.question: Which services already exist on this corridor?
services.summary: Intermodal and maritime services described one by one: route, stops, timetables, frequencies, operator and contacts.
covers: Each service keeps its pattern: one-way, round trip, loop, metro, looped metro.
services.mapAlt: Illustrative map of Europe: corridors of rail, waterway and sea services, whose thickness shows their density.

agent.collect: Picks up the services published by operators.
agent.normalize: Brings them to a single service record.

networks.name: Waterway and rail networks
networks.question: Does a link hold on the routes that exist?
networks.summary: Rivers, canals and railway lines, with their dimensions: navigation class, draught, maximum convoy, air draught.
covers: Each waterway is tied to its dimension class.
Nodes and inland ports connect the routes to terminals and services.
networks.mapAlt: Illustrative map of Europe: the main rivers and canals, coloured by navigation class.

agent.collect: Gathers waterway and rail line data.

points.name: Charging points and parkings
points.question: Where to charge, where to stop?
points.summary: Truck charging points and parking areas, with the status of each site, power, access, price and booking when known.
covers: Each site: in service, under construction or planned.
Charging points and their power, tied to the equipped corridors.
points.mapAlt: Illustrative map of Europe: charging points and truck parkings along the main corridors.

agent.collect: Picks up the published charging points and parkings.

carriers.name: Carriers
carriers.question: Who can carry out this transport?
carriers.summary: The listed carriers: their locations, their equipment, the reviews received and their contacts.
covers: Comparable records: equipment, areas covered, contacts.
Used to build the bid list of each tender.
carriers.mapAlt: Illustrative map of Europe: carrier locations and the areas they cover.

prices.name: Market prices
prices.question: At what price does the market carry out this transport?
prices.summary: Our cost models cross dozens of parameters with market data from contracts and spot databases, to compare every estimate with the prices actually charged.
covers: Each estimate is positioned against the distribution of market prices.
Choices and decisions rest on that positioning.

agent.collect: Gathers market data: contracts and spot databases.
